prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin corner from the same
camera position, the same wide vertical framing, the same young man in the
navy blue polo shirt and beige chinos standing with his back to us on the
grey cobbles behind the granite kerb, the same pedestrian traffic light on
its bare grey pole with the upper round lens glowing an even plain red, the
same pale cream facade, the same black city bicycles along the wall, the
same flat overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is on the road in front of him. Starting at the kerb where he
waits and running across the road away from the camera, a pedestrian crossing
of broad white bars is painted on the grey asphalt, the same bars as in the
second reference photograph. The red bicycle strip runs beside it on the
RIGHT, its dashed white edge between the two, so the crossing reads as two
lanes side by side: the white bars in front of him, the red strip to their
right.
